# V1b images (F-007b): human body organs, ~4 minutes, written in the style of the real-mic transcripts (fragments,
# one self-correction, one mis-hearing "a order" for "aorta"). Concrete organs (heart, lungs, digestive system,
# skeleton) where a picture helps; numbers and a breathing process where it does not.
Hello everyone, today we will learn about the human body and its main organs.
Let us start with the heart.
The heart is a muscular organ that pumps blood through the whole body.
It is about the size of your fist and it sits in the chest, slightly to the left.
[pause 1]
The heart has four chambers. The two upper chambers are called atria
and the two lower chambers are called ventricles.
The atria receive blood and the ventricles pump the blood out of the heart.
Blood leaves the left ventricle through the biggest artery called the a order.
[pause 1.5]
An adult heart beats about 72 times in a minute.
[pause 2]
Now let's talk about the lungs.
The lungs are two spongy organs in the chest where oxygen enters the blood.
When we breathe in, air enters through the nose,
then it passes down the windpipe,
then it goes into tiny air sacs called alveoli,
and from the alveoli oxygen passes into the blood.
[pause 1]
Carbon dioxide goes the other way and we breathe it out.
[pause 2]
Next is the digestive system.
Food is broken down in the mouth by chewing and by saliva.
The oesophagus is a muscular tube that pushes the food down to the stomach.
The stomach churns the food with acid and enzymes.
The small intestine absorbs most of the nutrients into the blood, and the large intestine absorbs the water.
[pause 2]
Finally, the skeleton.
An adult human skeleton has 206 bones, sorry, an adult has 206 bones and a baby has around 300.
The longest bone is the femur, in the thigh, and the smallest bone is the stapes, in the ear.
The skull protects the brain and the rib cage protects the heart and the lungs.
[pause 1]
So that is a short introduction to the main organs of the human body.
